item.title: Thursday, October 8, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk: One, stop quoting the weekly survey — the daily trackers have the thirty-year at or above 7.5% while Freddie Mac still says 7.28%, and a new Freddie Mac print lands at noon today; re-qualify every pre-approval written in August, because 60 basis points has moved the goalposts. Two, ask your lenders whether they are pricing the FHFA's bi-merge change, two credit reports instead of three — a real cost saving at application and a better read for thin-file buyers. Three, work the Jersey City versus Manhattan rent divergence alongside the New Jersey layoff file: Jersey City rents are falling because supply arrived, Manhattan's are at records because nobody can move, and September's notices in Princeton, Plainsboro and Hudson County will surface as relocation listings in roughly ninety days. Also in this episode: the 10-year Treasury at a 24-year high, divided FOMC minutes after September's hike to 3.75-4%, Hurricane Isaias bearing down on the Gulf Coast, the Hormuz tanker strike, Spain's housing decree, record-then-retreat equity markets, Verity's $32.6m box office win, the $111bn Skydance-Warner Bros Discovery close, and Real Madrid team news ahead of Villarreal.

item.title: Sunday, October 4, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One, the G train signal works begin Monday 5 October and run through 26 October, so Brooklyn showings on that corridor need rerouting now. Two, the New York City rent freeze is live as of 1 October, with stabilised renewals at zero percent on both one- and two-year leases through next September, so stabilised assets need re-underwriting and renewal notices need checking against the new order. Three, stop waiting for the Fed: its last move was a hike, a cut on 28 October is priced at roughly two percent, and Freddie Mac's weekly survey at 7.28 percent is already lagging a daily market at 7.57 percent, so lock what you can lock now. And three things for the world. One, Brazil votes today in the first round of its general election, with a runoff on 25 October if nobody clears fifty percent, Lula against Flavio Bolsonaro. Two, the United Arab Emirates has formally ruled the Flydubai cockpit attack an attempted terrorist act, with 174 people aboard the Dubai to Tel Aviv flight. Three, Tom Cruise's Digger opened at 7.5 million dollars against a budget of up to 160 million, one of the year's most expensive box office failures.

item.title: Thursday, October 1, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One: the ninth of October is the deadline — Portal North Bridge work cuts New York Penn Station service from 10 October through 15 November, and every weekday Midtown Direct train is rerouted to Hoboken, so move Manhattan showings and closings off those trains and warn commuting buyers now. Two: a new Freddie Mac survey prints today around midday; the last read 7.03 percent, and the gap to 6.30 percent a year ago is 242 dollars a month on a 500,000 dollar loan, so reprice affordability sheets the moment it lands. Three: Governor Sherrill's housing plan names Red Bank, Bayonne and Linden for transit-oriented development, doubles state-land production to 40,000 units and puts a shot clock on permits — set alerts on those towns and ask developer clients what a mandated approval timeline does to their option periods. And three things for the world. One: the Supreme Court has allowed deportations to third countries to resume while it weighs the policy, over the dissent of three justices. Two: the Federal Reserve raised rates unanimously on 16 September to a target range of 3.75 to 4 percent and said inflation remains elevated — the direction of travel is up, not down. Three: Brent crude is above 100 dollars a barrel, nearly 36 dollars higher than a year ago, the cleanest explanation of why the inflation fight is not finished.

item.title: Monday, September 28, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk: Quote the daily rate, not the weekly one — Mortgage News Daily had the 30-year fixed at 7.43% on Sept 25 against Freddie Mac's 7.03% weekly survey, a 40 basis point gap, and the daily figure is what your buyer's lock will reflect. The NAR commission settlement claims deadline is reportedly October 27 — verify it on the official litigation site this week and notify any client who transacted in the covered window. And split your pipeline by price band: KBW's downgrade of Lennar and upgrade of Toll Brothers says the entry-level buyer is the one who walks, so the bottom band needs a rate conversation and the top band does not. Also in this episode: the 10-year Treasury at 5.17% and a near-normal 186 basis point mortgage spread, meaning relief has to come from the bond market rather than from lenders; the Fed's September 16 hike to 3.75-4.00% with more signalled; the US-China $30 billion tariff product lists; the nor'easter that killed one and cut power to more than 130,000 across the Northeast; New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Dale Caldwell's resignation over an ethics and harassment report; a crowded box office led by an Avengers Endgame re-release at $26 million; and Real Madrid sitting second in La Liga on 15 points after the derby defeat at Atletico.

item.title: Thursday, September 24, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One: the daily thirty-year fixed is 7.26 percent, its highest since May 2024, and the ten-year Treasury hit 5.10 percent on Wednesday, a nineteen-year high, after moving nine basis points in a single session, so anyone floating a rate should be having the lock conversation today rather than next week. Two: Freddie Mac's weekly survey says 6.95 percent while the lock desk quotes 7.26 percent, and that gap needs explaining to every client before they find it themselves at the closing table. Three: Case-Shiller lands Tuesday the 29th and existing home sales have now fallen three months running to a 3.98 million annual pace, so have the line ready on why volume is falling faster than price, which is lock-in rather than a demand collapse. Also in this episode: the Fed's unanimous 25 basis point hike to 3.75 to 4.00 percent and a dot plot showing no return to 2 percent inflation until 2029, a wave of Manhattan office towers back on the sale market, the UN General Assembly high-level week, Lavrov ruling out a ceasefire, Wednesday's selloff across all four major indexes, Holtec pulling its IPO and Bristol Myers Squibb cutting 265 New Jersey jobs, a 60 million dollar opening for Resident Evil, and Valverde out roughly three weeks for Real Madrid.

item.title: Tuesday, September 22, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk: talk rate locks this week, because the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% and signalled one more, Freddie Mac is at 6.95% and the daily trackers are above 7%; warn commuter buyers about the Portal North Bridge cutover, which means fewer NJ Transit trains for about five weeks from October; and look at builder incentives, since Lennar's orders fell 9% and builders with slowing sales buy down rates. Also ask lenders whether VantageScore is now an option for thin-file borrowers. Three things for the world: the Fed's first hike since 2023; the UN General Assembly opens in New York, with a possible Trump-Zelenskyy meeting and President Xi arriving for a state visit; and big losses for Germany's political centre, with the AfD winning in the east and Die Linke winning Berlin.

item.title: Saturday, September 19, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk: rates moved against buyers and the move is not finished, with the 30-year fixed back above 7% after the Fed's first hike since 2023 and another hike live, so anyone floating into a closing inside 45 days should have the lock conversation now; housing completions fell 27.1% year over year in August, which is next year's inventory shortfall visible a full twelve months early and belongs in every hold-versus-sell conversation this quarter; and builder sentiment at 32 with Lennar cutting its full-year delivery target to 80,000-81,000 homes means new construction is where the negotiating leverage sits, with August existing and new home sales printing late next week. And three things for the world: the FOMC raised the federal funds target range to 3.75%-4.00% on 16 September, unanimously, under Chair Kevin Warsh; crude is holding above $95 a barrel and US diesel near $6.40 a gallon with the Strait of Hormuz under active attack, which is the inflation story behind the rate story; and the SEC approved a five-year conditional innovation exemption for tokenised assets, repricing the entire crypto complex in a single session.

item.title: Friday, September 18, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk this Friday, 18 September 2026. One: the Federal Reserve raised rates on Wednesday to a target range of 3.75 to 4.00 percent, and the daily 30-year mortgage now sits at 7.19 percent, just five basis points off its twelve-month high, while Freddie Mac's weekly survey still reads 6.95 percent — get ahead of that gap with clients before your lender has to explain it. Two: new home completions fell 27.1 percent year over year in August to an annual rate of 1,128,000, so builder incentives on finished stock are real right now but have a shelf life — a concrete reason for a hesitant buyer to move this autumn that does not depend on predicting rates. Three: KB Home reports third quarter results on Tuesday 22 September and the federal government funding deadline is 1 October; both can move sentiment inside two weeks. Also in this episode: August housing starts at 1,275,000 and the widening mortgage spread, Egypt's Sisi hosting Abbas in Cairo ahead of the UN General Assembly, the Supreme Court blocking mail ballot restrictions, Wednesday's equity close and the oil and gold moves, Practical Magic 2 taking the box office with 30 million dollars, and Real Madrid's 3-2 escape at Elche.

item.title: Tuesday, September 15, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk: Anchor property tax relief payments roll out in New Jersey this week, so get ahead of the client question. The Fed decides tomorrow afternoon and the market is pricing a hike rather than a cut, so anyone floating a rate today is taking a live position on it, and mind the gap between the 6.76 percent Freddie Mac survey your clients read in the paper and the 7.17 percent daily tracker they get quoted at the closing table. And New Jersey's August figures show supply up 6.9 percent and closed sales down 2.4 percent while homes still close at 101.8 percent of list, a seller's market loosening at the edges, so price to that rather than to last spring. And three things for the world: the Federal Reserve may raise rates tomorrow, with oil above 100 dollars a barrel the reason; the Iran war has moved into the shipping lanes, with a vessel struck in the Strait of Hormuz, Gulf talks postponed and a Saudi pipeline shut; and the AI slowdown argument went political in a single weekend, with Dario Amodei calling for a pause, Sam Altman, Elon Musk and Demis Hassabis agreeing, and the White House and the Speaker of the House saying no. Also inside: Emmy night, Monday's chip-led selloff, and Mourinho's Madrid past Rayo four-one.

item.title: Monday, September 14, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk: The Fed announces Wednesday with a fresh dot plot, and futures are pricing better-than-even odds of a hike rather than a cut, so ring your rate-locked buyers today rather than Thursday. The daily tracker has the thirty-year fixed at 6.88 percent while Freddie Mac's weekly survey says 6.76 percent, a twelve basis point gap that exists because the survey is weighted to Monday-through-Wednesday responses and missed the late-week back-up in yields, so have that explanation ready before a client quotes you the lower number. Manhattan's top end signed just thirteen luxury contracts in the week before Labor Day with nothing above ten million dollars, so price a trophy listing to the Fed this week, not to the spring. And three things for the world: oil is back above one hundred dollars a barrel with American diesel at a record six dollars and six cents a gallon, which is the inflation story sitting underneath the Fed's problem; a Russian drone struck the Kyiv-to-Warsaw train near the Polish border in a nationwide barrage that killed six and injured forty-three; and Sweden's centre-left has won by a single seat, leaving the far-right Sweden Democrats apparently locked out of government. Also inside: a 785 million dollar Manhattan office loan to special servicing against a 131 million dollar Nutley office trade, Oracle's 95 billion dollar capex lifting Dell and HPE, Practical Magic 2 topping a quiet 81.6 million dollar box office weekend, and Real Madrid 4-1 Rayo Vallecano with a Mbappe double.

item.title: Sunday, September 13, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One: the Federal Reserve decides at two o'clock on Wednesday the sixteenth — no cut is expected and some forecasters still see a hike, so any client sitting on a float needs to choose before Wednesday, not after. Two: requote everybody — the daily tracker is at 7.12 percent while the Freddie Mac headline says 6.76 percent, and that 36 basis point gap is the most likely source of an awkward conversation this week. Three: existing home sales fell 2 percent in August to a 3.98 million annual rate, below the four-million mark, with inventory building — sellers need a pricing conversation now, not in October. And three things for the world. One: core inflation fell to 2.4 percent, the lowest since March 2021, but headline inflation is stuck at 3.4 percent on petrol prices. Two: Saudi Arabia has shut its main East-West pipeline after drone strikes launched from Iraqi territory, with Iran the prime suspect, just as oil had been falling. Three: the eighteenth BRICS summit is under way in New Delhi with India in the chair, and the US-brokered Israel-Lebanon talks have slipped to October.

item.title: Saturday, September 12, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk today. First, and this is the deadline, the Federal Open Market Committee meets Wednesday the sixteenth and the market now puts a quarter point rate hike at ninety percent after Friday's inflation report, up from seventy percent the day before, so spend Monday and Tuesday on your rate sensitive pipeline and lock everything that can be locked before the committee speaks. Second, your clients are reading six point seven six percent from Thursday's Freddie Mac survey while daily quotes stood at six point nine eight percent annual percentage rate on Friday, up nineteen basis points in a single day, so explain the difference between a note rate and an annual percentage rate to every active buyer this week before the lock desk explains it for you. Third, the ten year Treasury closed the week at four point nine six percent, a fifty two week high, and the mortgage to Treasury spread is back to a historically normal one hundred and eighty basis points, so there is no abnormal spread left to deflate: underwrite new deals to a seven handle, and with existing home sales down two percent in August, price new listings to sell rather than to test the market. And three things for the world. First, yesterday was the twenty fifth anniversary of the September the eleventh attacks, marked at Ground Zero, the Pentagon and Shanksville. Second, American inflation is running at three point four percent a year, hotter than forecast, with gasoline up twenty seven point four percent over the year doing more than a third of the monthly damage. Third, Brent crude closed a week above one hundred dollars a barrel for the first time since May on Middle Eastern tension, which is precisely why the inflation number looked the way it did. Also in this episode: core inflation at two point four percent, the National Association of Realtors reporting August existing home sales down two percent, industrial commercial mortgage backed securities issuance picking up, Friday's market rebound inside a losing week, Real Madrid beating Inter Milan two goals to one to open the Champions League, and New Jersey's Governor under pressure over allegations against her Lieutenant Governor.

item.title: Thursday, September 10, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk today. First, the Federal Reserve meets Wednesday the sixteenth and markets put a rate hike at better than a coin flip, around fifty-six percent on CME FedWatch, so ring your rate-sensitive buyers and lock anything that can be locked before the meeting rather than after it. item.title: Saturday, September 5, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One, the deadline: the 25th anniversary of September 11th falls this Friday, with an expanded New York City commemoration and heavy security in Lower Manhattan, so move or pad any downtown showings, closings or client meetings now rather than Thursday night. Two, change your rate script: the 30-year fixed is at 6.71 percent, a 13-month high, and the spread over the 10-year Treasury has compressed to roughly 194 basis points, close to historically normal, so the free improvement is gone and further mortgage relief now requires the 10-year itself to fall, which Friday's hot jobs print pushes against.
